title: Alive, once alive or never alive

steps.say: Living things move, grow, feed, sense and have young. They also need air and water.
steps.show: move, grow, feed, sense, have young

steps.say: A tree is alive now. It grows and makes seeds.
Some things were once alive. Wood, paper and feathers came from living things.

figure.alt: Things that were once alive: a wooden spoon, paper and a feather.

steps.say: Some things were never alive. Stone, metal and glass were never part of a living thing.

figure.alt: Things that were never alive: a stone, a metal key and a glass.

steps.say: Moving is not enough to be alive. A car moves, but it cannot grow or have young.

options.why: Glass is made from sand, which was never alive.

hints: Once alive means it came from a living thing.
Think about where each material comes from.
Ask: which one came from a tree?
check.explanation: A wooden spoon is made of wood, which came from a living tree. So it was once alive.

options.why: Clouds move, but they never grow or have young.
A toy car cannot grow or have young.
A kite only moves when the wind blows it.

hints: Some living things look like they do nothing.
Ask: could it grow if it got water and warmth?
Think about planting each one in soil.
check.explanation: A seed is alive. When it gets water and warmth, it grows into a new plant.
